rules.title: Civil Rights Council regulations limiting use of criminal history in housing decisions
rules.requirement: Landlords face limits on what criminal history they may seek, how they may consider it, and what actions they may take based on it. Blanket bans on applicants with criminal records and policies that consider arrests without convictions are prohibited.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record bans; arrests without conviction may not be considered
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers in California screening rental applicants
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council (formerly Fair Employment and Housing Council) criminal history housing regulations (specific CCR section not given in source)
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source; regulation section numbers not cited in the document.

rules.title: SB 329: Source-of-income protection includes housing subsidies (Section 8)
rules.requirement: FEHA's definition of source of income includes government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8, so landlords may not refuse to participate in such programs or maintain 'No Section 8' policies.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords subject to the California Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.penalty: Enforcement by California Civil Rights Department, including lawsuits
rules.citation: SB 329 (2019), amending Fair Employment and Housing Act (Cal. Gov. Code)
rules.quoted_span: This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.

rules.title: SB 267: Credit history limits for applicants with government rental subsidies
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy (e.g., Section 8) without offering the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental property owners screening applicants who receive a government rental subsidy

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to applicants who have a government rental subsidy such as Section 8

rules.citation: SB 267, amending Fair Employment and Housing Act (Cal. Gov. Code)
rules.quoted_span: In addition, last year’s SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.conflict_note: Document says 'last year's SB 267' without an article date; enactment year and effective date not stated. Under California default rule it would take effect January 1 following enactment.
